seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Mid-July through September, within the broader late-spring-to-October window

July.reason: Brush and rock are typically dry and passable, long daylight hours help with the long, slow off-trail sections

June.reason: Lingering snow patches possible on the upper ridge in higher-snow years, and brush is leafing out and at its thickest, compounding the already-brushy approach

August.reason: Driest and most reliable conditions of the season, though this is also when afternoon thunderstorms are most common

October.reason: Early snow or sustained rain can arrive, wet brush and rock significantly slow and add risk to the already loose, routefinding-heavy terrain

September.reason: Stable weather and cooler temps typical, brush begins dying back which can ease travel, but shorter days trim margin for a long brushy day

before.best_season: This is treated as much as a winter/early-season snowshoe objective as a summer scramble. Roughly November through April, consolidated snow bridges the worst slide-alder brush and boulder fields on the west ridge, though it demands snowshoes, an ice axe, and solid routefinding in what is often fog/whiteout terrain. A July-September ascent is driest underfoot but means fighting through dense brush and downed timber the whole way. Avoid the shoulder season (roughly late April-May) when snow on the boulder fields tends to be rotten/isothermal and hides holes.
before.rope_note: Class 2 off-trail scramble up steep western slopes from Lake Serene; best May/June when snow covers underbrush. No technical gear.
